verdicts.name: p_merged
verdicts.note: Per-contact trial fractions are pooled as though they were binary trial outcomes.

verdicts.name: dose_at_1e-6
verdicts.note: The first qualifying sampled dose is reported unresolved when no downward crossing occurs between sampled doses.

logic.text: The exposure-dose grid is generated as an evenly spaced sequence that differs from the plan's grid.
logic.note: The requested dose sweep is not evaluated at all its specified settings.
logic.fix: Use the plan's explicit dose list.
logic.name: exposure_dose_grid

logic.text: The aerial image is divided by the source-point count after its maximum has already been normalized.
logic.note: This changes photon arrival rates according to the number of illumination samples and makes the line and contact exposures incomparable.
logic.fix: Normalize the source average once to the declared aerial-intensity convention.
logic.name: mean_absorbed_photons

logic.text: The source coordinates do not implement the specified dipole pole radius or annular radial bounds.
logic.note: Both aerial images use different illumination settings from those stated in the method.
logic.fix: Sample the specified dipole disks and contact annulus, and apply source-radius changes to those geometries.

logic.text: The quencher is a newly sampled Poisson field at each trial and dose.
logic.note: The plan defines a fixed quencher field relative to a reference-dose mean acid density.
logic.fix: Construct the fixed quencher field from a declared reference dose and subtract that same field for every dose.
logic.name: LER

logic.text: The reference dose is set to the current exposure dose.
logic.note: Dose-dependent thresholds and quenching then track the exposure rather than using a fixed calibration, changing the intended dose response.
logic.fix: Define and retain a separate calibration reference dose for the threshold and quencher laws.
logic.name: p_missing

logic.text: The classifier minimum width is passed to the line classifier but never used.
logic.note: The requested classifier sensitivity cannot affect bridge or break results.
logic.fix: Apply the selected minimum neck or gap width when testing connectivity.
logic.name: p_bridge

logic.text: Any absent center pixel marks a line break.
logic.note: A connected line can move away from the center and remain topologically intact.
logic.fix: Classify breaks from connectivity of the intended line across the segment, with the selected minimum width.
logic.name: p_break

logic.text: The trial returns only whether its roughness is defined, not the number of printable and excluded segments.
logic.note: The reported printable fraction and excluded defect count cannot be formed reliably from the returned fields.
logic.fix: Return printable and excluded segment counts and aggregate them in the experiment result.
logic.name: printable_fraction

logic.text: Neither printed line width nor printed contact diameter is returned.
logic.note: Dose-to-size requires ensemble means of those measurements.
logic.fix: Measure each printable feature's size and return the measurements for aggregation and interpolation.
logic.name: dose_to_size

logic.text: The sum of per-contact fractions is truncated to an integer and divided by the number of trials.
logic.note: The fractions represent multiple contacts per trial, so this produces incorrect contact probabilities and Wilson intervals.
logic.fix: Return contact event counts and contact totals from each trial, then pool those counts for the probability and interval.
logic.name: p_missing

logic.text: Threshold crossing requires a transition from above the target at one sampled dose to below it at the next.
logic.note: A range beginning below the target has a supported first sampled dose but is labeled unresolved.
logic.fix: Handle an initially qualifying dose separately and interpolate only when a bracketing pair exists.
logic.name: dose_at_1e-6

logic.text: The common dose interval is initialized to an empty list and never changed.
logic.note: The result is constant regardless of the four supported defect intervals.
logic.fix: Intersect the supported intervals for all defect classes and report the resulting common interval.
logic.name: common_interval_mJ_cm2

checked: R31–R33: The trial grid includes both resist types, both patterns, and both chemistry settings.
R34–R39: The uniform-region branch returns every field named by the specified check measures and partitions incident photons into absorbed and transmitted counts.
R40–R41: The marked E1 and E2 functions use the plan's factors and consistent inverse-nanometre absorption units.
The marked E3 and E4 functions implement the stated relative-noise and zero-event formulas.
The uniform-region branch samples incident Poisson counts and independently thins them for absorption.
The CAR branch samples acid yield conditional on absorbed events and applies the electron and diffusion Gaussian blurs.
The MOR branch applies its single Gaussian blur before threshold development.
The roughness summary bootstraps trial-level values, as specified for independent line realizations.
The line-defect probability summary applies Wilson intervals to binary trial outcomes.
